market_summary: US stocks had their worst week in more than 18 months: the S&P 500 and Dow are in correction, and the Nasdaq-100 is down about 10.5% on the week, near bear territory. Futures bounced Sunday night, with the S&P +2% and the Nasdaq-100 +2.8%. Rates are a headwind: markets still lean towards a Fed hike in December, and the 10-year yield rose about 4bp overnight. Doubts about returns on AI capex and the Nvidia probes drove the selloff, yet AI server prices are up as much as 45%, so demand has not broken. Brent fell 0.8% while European gas rose as much as 8.6%. China cut its margin requirement to 80% to prop up stocks.
